summary: Initial discovery for Dedicated capacity. Montara has strict data isolation needs and predictable peak traffic for a fraud-detection real-time inference product. Main concerns: latency SLOs at 50-100ms p50 for short prompts, predictable reserved throughput, burst handling, VPC networking, and compliance (SOC2, KMS). Redwood AE/SE outlined Dedicated architecture, autoscaling/burst policies, private deployment options, observable metrics, and pilot steps.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh this is Alex from Redwood, I have Samir our solutions engineer and Lena from success, um we'll run through questions and then dig into your workloads.
[00:12] Jenna Morales: Thanks Alex. We appreciate it. I'll let Marcus and Priya intro. Marcus?
[00:17] Marcus Lee: Hey all, Marcus, Head of ML at Montara. We're building a real-time fraud model endpoint for transaction scoring. Need high throughput during batch windows and low latency for inline scoring.
[00:28] Priya Singh: Priya here, security. I'll be focused on data residency, encryption, and audit requirements.
[00:34] Daniel Park: Daniel, infra. We'll own the VPC/network side.
[00:38] Alex Chen: Great. Quick agenda: confirm traffic/SLAs, isolation needs (hosted vs dedicated vs private), burst & scaling expectations, and then next steps for pilot. Sound good?
[00:48] Jenna Morales: Yep. Our core ask: can you guarantee predictable throughput and isolation? We can't have noisy neighbors on public hosted.
[00:55] Samir Gupta: Totally. For that we recommend Dedicated — reserved GPU pools with configurable burst. So you get capacity isolation, and you can pin models and versions.
[01:04] Marcus Lee: What does "burst" mean operationally? Like if we have big batch jobs at night can we exceed reserved capacity?
[01:10] Samir Gupta: Good question. There's two knobs: reserved baseline capacity and burst buffers. With Dedicated you commit to reserved GPUs for steady-state. We can allow burst capacity to spin up additional nodes in the same cluster if capacity available; burst is typically metered and has configurable throttles. It's not unlimited; it's subject to region/global availability.
[01:24] Daniel Park: Is bursting inside our network or does that route to shared cloud infra? We need to know about egress paths for compliance.
[01:31] Alex Chen: If you go Dedicated in our managed offering, the compute is reserved to your tenant but still run in Redwood-managed infra; network egress paths can be peered into your VPC. For a fully private deployment (on-prem or VPC private control plane) compute lives in your environment. We'll send the network diagram examples.
[01:46] Priya Singh: We need encryption at rest and KMS support, and an audit trail for model access. Can you integrate with our KMS/HSM?
[01:53] Samir Gupta: Yes, we have KMS integrations for major clouds and an HSM option for private deployments. Audit logs and token-level tracing are supported in Redwood Console. We'll share SOC2 artifacts and the security pack.
[02:05] Marcus Lee: Latency — we're targeting p50 <= 80ms for 256-token-ish prompt sizes. Is that realistic on Dedicated?
[02:11] Samir Gupta: Depends on model choice and batching. For smaller encoder-decoder style models or optimized LLMs with quantization you can hit that, especially with continuous batching and KV cache. For generative models with longer contexts 80ms is tight but doable with right model. We should benchmark your specific prompt sizes.
[02:24] Jenna Morales: We're evaluating models from open-source and also a custom fine-tuned model. We want the model lifecycle: pinning versions and rollbacks.
[02:31] Samir Gupta: Dedicated supports version pinning and canary rollouts. You can designate a primary pool for production and a canary pool for testing new variants.
[02:37] Marcus Lee: What about cost — reserved capacity vs hosted? We don't want cost surprises from bursts.
[02:42] Alex Chen: Reserved capacity gives predictability; bursts are billed separately by metered units. We can tailor the contract: a base commit + capped burst spend, or prioritized burst windows. We'll include example billing scenarios in the pricing doc.
[02:53] Priya Singh: Any customers using private deployment for regulated workloads?
[02:57] Alex Chen: Yes, a few banks and healthcare orgs run private control plane in their VPC or on-prem. We have templates for compliance controls and an on-prem installer for air-gapped setups.
[03:07] Marcus Lee: For pilot: what's a minimal successful pilot?
[03:10] Samir Gupta: Typically a 2-week pilot: we replicate representative traffic, run end-to-end inference with pinned model, run latency and throughput tests, and validate observability and audit logs. If you own infra for private pilot, we can run the same harness there.
[03:23] Jenna Morales: What telemetry do we get? We need token-level cost, per-route latency, and error traces.
[03:29] Alex Chen: Redwood Console surfaces token-level cost, p50/p95/p99, per-model dashboards, request traces and error logs. We also emit metrics to CloudWatch/Prometheus if you want to ingest.
[03:40] Daniel Park: About networking — we prefer VPC peering with no NAT and strict egress controls. Is SAML/SSO supported?
[03:47] Samir Gupta: Yes SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC for teams, and VPC peering is supported in Dedicated and Private topologies. For fully private deployments you'll control all network egress.
[03:56] Marcus Lee: For the model itself, we'll likely use a 7B-ish fine-tuned model. Do you recommend quantization?
[04:02] Samir Gupta: For 7B that's a sweet spot for int8 or nf4 quantization — big win on cost with modest latency improvements. We can provide recommended quant profiles based on your accuracy SLA.
[04:12] Jenna Morales: Are there limits on concurrent requests per GPU? We need to size for peak QPS and also low p50 latency.
[04:18] Samir Gupta: Concurrency depends on model and token length. We size GPUs for target latency under expected token budgets and use batching to increase throughput. We'll ask for your qps distribution (p50/p95 peaks, tokens per request) — that'll let us propose reserved GPU counts.
[04:32] Alex Chen: Could you share a rough qps?
[04:34] Marcus Lee: Baseline 80 qps during business hours, peak 400 qps for short bursts during settlement windows; average tokens per request ~40, some longer investigative runs ~800 tokens but much lower frequency.
[04:49] Samir Gupta: Nice. With that profile, initial sizing might be 4-8 GPUs reserved plus a burst buffer; exact number depends on model and batching. We'll run the benchmark.
[04:59] Priya Singh: For audit, we need immutable logs of model inferences tied to request ids and user ids. Can we redact PII prior to logging?
[05:07] Samir Gupta: You can configure the platform to redact or hash fields before logs are persisted; we also support custom preprocessing hooks if you need to strip PII.
[05:15] Jenna Morales: Regarding failure modes — what happens if reserved capacity is exhausted? Does traffic queue or failover to hosted smaller models?
[05:24] Alex Chen: You can set fallback policies: queue with backpressure, degrade to a smaller model variant, or spill to hosted (with data egress considerations). Many customers configure automatic fallback to a cheaper, lower-latency variant for non-critical paths.
[05:37] Marcus Lee: We want to avoid sending sensitive payloads to shared hosted endpoints. If fallback to hosted is an option we need to ensure data never leaves our VPC.
[05:44] Alex Chen: Understood — for that use-case, a private deployment or Dedicated with strict no-fallback-to-hosted policy is recommended; we can also provide regional, single-tenant nodes.
[05:55] Daniel Park: What's the SLA on Dedicated latency and uptime?
[05:59] Alex Chen: Uptime SLAs are contractual; latency SLOs depend on model and infra. We provide observable SLOs in the console and can set contractual targets for 99.9% availability. We'll propose target SLOs in the pilot plan.
[06:12] Samir Gupta: Also worth calling out: intelligent batching and prefix caching can dramatically lower per-token cost for repeated prompts — if your workload has repetitiveness we can tune caching.
[06:23] Jenna Morales: Our transaction scoring has many repeated merchant-context prompts, so prefix caching could help.
[06:28] Alex Chen: We'll include an expected cost delta with cache and quantization applied in the pricing doc.
[06:35] Marcus Lee: For the pilot harness — will you run the inference inside our VPC or in Redwood-managed infra?
[06:40] Samir Gupta: Either. For quick pilos (pilots), the fastest is Redwood-managed Dedicated reserved GPUs with VPC peering. For compliance-heavy pilots, we deploy the harness into your VPC/private deployment.
[06:53] Priya Singh: If we do an on-prem pilot, what kind of engineer support is required?
[06:57] Samir Gupta: We'll provide an on-prem installer and SE guidance. Expect 1-2 infra engineers from your side to help with networking/storage initially. We'll run most of the integration remotely.
[07:08] Alex Chen: Any blockers on timeline?
[07:11] Jenna Morales: Need budget approval, but we want pilot next sprint if possible; timeline ~2-3 weeks to decide.
[07:18] Alex Chen: Great we can aim for pilot in 2 weeks. Samir, hey can you send the benchmark template and pilot plan?
[07:24] Samir Gupta: Yep, I'll share the spreadsheet and a recommended load generator setup. I'll also include our sample network diagram and the security pack.
[07:31] Daniel Park: On the subject of IAM, we need SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and SSO.
[07:36] Alex Chen: Supported — we'll include integration docs.
[07:40] Marcus Lee: A couple quick technical clarifications: how do you handle KV cache invalidation across model versions?
[07:46] Samir Gupta: Cache tied to model version; when you roll out a new version we can cascade a cache warm-up policy or invalidate. That avoids stale states.
[07:55] Jenna Morales: We also want to run internal A/B tests; is traffic split supported?
[07:59] Samir Gupta: Yes, canary and A/B rollout traffic splits are natively supported.
[08:04] Priya Singh: Anything special we need for logging HIPAA-equivalent data? Not HIPAA but similar regs.
[08:10] Alex Chen: We'll map compliance controls and share our compliance pack; private deployment gives you full control if needed.
[08:16] Jenna Morales: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[08:19] Alex Chen: Recap: Alex to send pricing + example SKUs and SLA, Samir to send benchmark template and pilot plan, Montara to share qps distribution, network diagram, and compliance contact. We'll schedule a technical deep dive next week.
[08:35] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:38] Alex Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.

Note: minor transcription artifacts and speaker overlaps occur; some product names may be slightly transcribed (e.g., Redwood Console sometimes as "Redwood console").
